title: Zillow calls itself “AI-native.” It just cut 500 jobs and won’t say whether AI was the reason.
excerpt: Zillow cut more than 500 jobs, its biggest layoff of the year, a day before earnings. The self-styled "AI-native" firm won't say whether AI drove it.
content_html:
Zillow laid off more than 500 people on Tuesday, about 7% of its staff and its largest cut of the year. The Seattle property company made the move one day before it reports quarterly earnings. It has spent the year telling investors it is becoming an “AI-native” company. It will not say whether AI had anything to do with the cuts.

Chief executive Jeremy Wacksman framed the decision as housekeeping. In a blog post, he said it was about “ensuring we have a disciplined cost structure and getting more efficient, with the right people in the right positions,” and little else. Growing at scale means the company must “work differently than we do today,” he wrote.

Growing and cutting at once

What makes this awkward is that Zillow is not struggling. First-quarter revenue rose 18% to $708m, GeekWire reported, against an industry growing just 2%. Profit jumped to $46m from $8m a year earlier. Wacksman says the company keeps outperforming a flat housing market.

So the cut looks less like a rescue and more like a squeeze on costs. Zillow has been spending heavily on rental listings, loan officers, advertising and legal bills. It told investors in May that spending would ease in the second half. Payroll is one of the faster ways to make that happen, and its earnings guidance on Wednesday may show it.

The AI question it won’t answer

The silence on AI is conspicuous. In April, Wacksman told real-estate executives that Zillow was retraining staff to use AI, with gains that were “small, but they’re compounding,” Real Estate News reported. In May, he went further on an earnings call: “We are rapidly becoming an AI-native company.”

Yet asked directly whether AI shaped Tuesday’s layoffs, the company said nothing. Both GeekWire and Real Estate News put the question to it. Neither got an answer. That reticence is now a pattern. AI has become the reason companies most often give for cutting jobs, and the reason many are careful not to give.

Zillow is not alone in the dance. Patreon cut a fifth of its staff while its boss insisted AI was not the cause. Monday.com trimmed jobs even as it grew. It fits a broader wave of tech cuts where firms hedge on whether the technology is doing the cutting.

Pressure from other directions

There is more than efficiency at play. Zillow’s shares have fallen more than 47% this year despite the strong results, a gap the finance chief called a “dislocation,” or temporary mispricing. Law firms are trawling for shareholders to join a proposed class action. This month it goes to trial in an FTC antitrust case over a $100m deal for exclusive rental listings on Redfin’s sites.

The wider property-tech sector is contracting too. CoStar has cut its Homes.com sales team, Better’s founder stepped down as chief executive this week, and Rocket trimmed staff after buying Redfin. Whether or not AI is quietly reshaping these companies, the industry is rethinking how many people it needs. Zillow’s earnings on Wednesday will show how deep the discipline goes.

content_html_zh:
Zillow 周二解雇了 500 多人，约占员工总数的 7%，是今年最大的一次裁员。 这家西雅图房地产公司在公布季度收益的前一天采取了这一举措。 该公司花了一年的时间告诉投资者，它正在成为一家“人工智能本土”公司。 它不会说人工智能是否与削减有任何关系。

首席执行官杰里米·瓦克斯曼 (Jeremy Wacksman) 将这一决定视为“内政管理”。 他在一篇博客文章中表示，这是为了“确保我们拥有严格的成本结构并提高效率，让合适的人担任合适的职位”，除此之外别无其他。 他写道，大规模增长意味着公司必须“以不同于我们今天的方式运作”。

一次生长和切割

令人尴尬的是 Zillow 并没有挣扎。 据 GeekWire 报道，第一季度收入增长 18%，达到 7.08 亿美元，而整个行业仅增长 2%。 利润从一年前的 800 万美元跃升至 4600 万美元。 瓦克斯曼表示，该公司的表现一直优于平淡的房地产市场。

因此，此次削减看起来不像是一次救援，而更像是压缩成本。 Zillow 一直在租赁清单、信贷员、广告和法律费用上投入巨资。 它在五月份告诉投资者，下半年支出将放缓。 薪资是实现这一目标的最快方法之一，周三的盈利指引可能会证明这一点。

人工智能无法回答的问题

对人工智能的沉默是显而易见的。 据《房地产新闻》报道，今年 4 月，瓦克斯曼告诉房地产高管，Zillow 正在对员工使用人工智能进行再培训，其收益“虽小，但正在复合增长”。 五月份，他在财报电话会议上进一步说道：“我们正在迅速成为一家人工智能本土公司。”

然而，当被直接问及人工智能是否影响了周二的裁员时，该公司什么也没说。 GeekWire 和房地产新闻都提出了这个问题。 两人都没有得到答案。 这种沉默现在已成为一种模式。 人工智能已经成为公司最常给出的裁员理由，也是许多公司谨慎不给出的理由。

Zillow 并不是唯一一个参与其中的人。 Patreon 裁掉了五分之一的员工，而其老板坚称人工智能不是原因。 Monday.com 在扩张的同时也削减了工作岗位。 它适合更广泛的技术削减浪潮，企业对冲技术是否正在削减成本。

来自其他方向的压力

发挥作用的不仅仅是效率。 尽管业绩强劲，但 Zillow 的股价今年仍下跌了 47% 以上，财务负责人称这种差距为“错位”，即暂时的定价错误。 律师事务所正在寻找股东加入拟议的集体诉讼。 本月，联邦贸易委员会 (FTC) 反垄断案件将接受审判，该案件涉及 Redfin 网站上一项价值 1 亿美元的独家租赁清单交易。

更广泛的房地产科技行业也在萎缩。 CoStar 削减了 Homes.com 销售团队，Better 创始人本周辞去首席执行官职务，Rocket 在收购 Redfin 后裁员。 无论人工智能是否正在悄然重塑这些公司，该行业都在重新思考它需要多少人才。 Zillow 周三的财报将显示该纪律的深入程度。
